description: Call this right after each payment succeeds, with the rail's own reference (a merchant calls it for each payment received, with direction inflow). Records the payment: sealed, matched to its intent, checked against its cap and expiry. The same payment again returns unchanged. Different facts for a payment already sealed return conflict and seal nothing, unless you give correction: { reason }.

buyer_authentication.description: Optional: how the buyer proved it was them at checkout. Never the evidence itself

reference.description: The authentication's own reference, such as the 3-D Secure transaction ID

result.description: authenticated, attempted, failed and so on

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the authentication evidence, kept elsewhere

buyer_intent.description: For a merchant recording a payment it received: the buyer's own sealed intent ({ payload, seal }) as the buyer's agent presented it at checkout. It must check with buyer_key; the record keeps its hash and whether the payment was inside it

buyer_key.description: The buyer's public key, to check buyer_intent

correction.description: Only to correct a payment already sealed: the new version says why

reason.description: Why the sealed record was wrong

counterparty_id.description: Optional: how the payee is identified, as scheme:value, such as domain:data.example or wallet:0x…

counterparty_type.description: Optional: organization, person, service or agent

evidence_type.description: Optional: onchain for a blockchain transaction, provider_reference for a payment provider's reference

invoice_ref.description: Optional: the invoice or bill number this payment paid, as given to check_payment

network.description: Optional: the network it settled on, such as base or solana

occurred_at.description: When the rail says the payment was made, in ISO 8601 with its offset (2026-10-28T19:00:00Z or 2026-10-28T12:00:00-07:00)

order_id.description: Optional: the merchant's order ID for this payment, as the merchant shows it (on the receipt or order confirmation)

processor_transaction_id.description: Optional: the payment processor's own transaction ID (Stripe, Adyen, the acquirer), where it differs from source_id. Both can be added later to a record already sealed

receipt.description: Optional: where the receipt or invoice is kept, and its hash; never the receipt itself

settlement_provider.description: Optional: who settled the payment, such as the x402 facilitator

source_id.description: The rail's own reference: transaction hash, charge ID

name: record_settlement
